title: Evaluating Video LLMs' Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving
abstract: arXiv:2611.16767v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Natural language explanations promised by modern Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) offer autonomous driving systems a path toward detailed scene description and interpretable decision making on the road. While recent benchmarks have begun assessing these models on driving scenes, they mainly target routine traffic conditions and general comprehension tasks based on existing driving datasets and therefore fail to evaluate model performance on the rarest and most safety-critical driving events, also known as "corner cases". To provide a comprehensive evaluation of Video LLMs on precisely these scenarios, we introduce DashBench, a benchmark testing 25 Video LLMs on 1,709 carefully curated driving videos spanning not only collision-related corner cases but also rare non-collision ones. translated_title: 评估视频大语言模型对自动驾驶中边缘案例的理解能力
translated_abstract: 现代视频大语言模型所承诺的自然语言解释能力，为自动驾驶系统提供了一条实现详细场景描述和可解释道路决策的路径。尽管近期的基准测试已经开始在驾驶场景上评估这些模型，但它们主要针对常规交通状况以及基于现有驾驶数据集的一般性理解任务，因此无法评估模型在最罕见、最关乎安全的驾驶事件（即“边缘案例”）上的表现。为了对视频大语言模型在这些场景上的表现进行全面的评估，我们推出了DashBench，该基准在1,709个精心筛选的驾驶视频上测试了25个视频大语言模型，这些视频不仅涵盖与碰撞相关的边缘案例，还包括罕见的非碰撞边缘案例。通过大量的提示词和开放式问答，我们揭示了一个关键的能力差距：所有被评估的模型的表现都显著低于……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 提出DashBench基准，利用1,709个涵盖碰撞及罕见非碰撞边缘案例的驾驶视频对25个视频大语言模型进行测试，揭示出这些模型在理解自动驾驶中安全关键的罕见场景方面存在显著的能力差距。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces DashBench, a benchmark testing 25 Video LLMs on 1,709 curated driving videos covering both collision-related and rare non-collision corner cases, revealing a critical capability gap in models' understanding of safety-critical rare driving scenarios.
